headline: Evaluating Solar Installation During a Remodel
articleBody: Solar installation should be evaluated as both an electrical project and a roofing or structural project, especially when it is added during a remodel. The California Energy Commission and local permitting authorities require compliant electrical design, proper interconnection, and adherence to building and fire standards. In practice, that means a solar installer must coordinate with the roofing contractor, electrician, and sometimes the structural engineer to ensure the roof can support the system and the wiring is safely routed. For Los Angeles County homeowners, the key comparison points are equipment quality, inverter configuration, roof penetration strategy, warranty coverage, and whether the installer handles permit and utility approval. The National Renewable Energy Laboratory notes that design decisions affect performance, maintenance, and lifecycle value, not just upfront price. Buyers should ask if the company will perform a site assessment that considers shading, roof age, electrical panel capacity, and future battery storage. If the roof is near end of life, many owners choose to replace the roof before installing solar to avoid later system removal and reinstall costs. Because solar incentives and interconnection rules can change, the contractor should be able to explain the current permitting sequence without making financial promises outside the scope of installation. The strongest proposals are the ones that separate solar equipment, roof work, electrical upgrades, and monitoring hardware so the owner can see where the cost is coming from.
